gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a 48V inverter running at its full 6–6.5 kW pulls about 127–141 A from a 51.2 V battery bank (6,500 W ÷ 51.2 V = 127 A before losses, about 141 A at 90% efficiency). That is why Sun Gold Power's own 6,500 W + one-battery kit ships with a 160 A DC breaker and 4 AWG cable. ChatGPT's pairing of 'one 51.2V 100Ah battery + a 5–6 kW inverter' with a lump-sum '$200–$800 DC protection' never names the current the cable, breaker and battery must carry.
standout_why: ChatGPT got no search results in either saved chat, so there were no rival pages to compare against. I compared against ChatGPT's two answers. They give price ranges for battery, inverter and DC protection, and name EG4, Sol-Ark and Victron as inverter brands. They never give the DC current at full inverter output, a breaker or cable size, how many 100Ah packs a 6 kW inverter needs, or the fact that a split-phase inverter/charger needs a 240 V feed to charge and pass power through. Scored 2, not 3: I could not open a page confirming the SG48100P's battery-side continuous current limit, and that number is what would decide one pack versus two.
kit_items: inverter/charger: Sun Gold Power 6000W 48V Split Phase Pure Sine Wave Inverter with Charger (UL1741). It has a built-in charger and AC auto-transfer switch and outputs 120/240 V, which fits grid-charged outage backup with no solar.
alternative inverter if solar is planned: Sun Gold Power SPH6548P 6.5 kW 48V split-phase hybrid. It adds 2 MPPT solar inputs and up to 140 A battery charging, and costs less ($1,035).

battery: Sun Gold Power SG48100P 51.2V 100Ah server-rack LiFePO4 (UL1973/UL9540A, CAN/RS485/RS232), bought as the 2-pack (10.24 kWh). Two packs share the roughly 130–140 A a 6 kW inverter draws at full load. The maker sells the pair as its own SKU.

DC protection and cabling: a DC breaker of about 160 A between the battery and the inverter, and 4 AWG or heavier cable. These are the sizes Sun Gold Power ships in its SGM-655M 6,500 W kit. With two batteries, add a busbar and 1/0 AWG battery cables, as the SGM-6510M kit does.

transfer/connection: an electrician-installed 2-pole 240 V feed into the inverter's AC input and a protected-loads subpanel on its output. Sun Gold Power's page says the split-phase inverter 'requires 240VAC input', so it cannot charge from a 120 V wall outlet.
